Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

RMediation 1.9.0 (2026-10-31)

The ci(type = "asymp") interval label changes (see Behavior changes); two silent-wrong-value density bugs are fixed.

Behavior changes

  • ci(type = "asymp") now names its interval by its confidence level, 100 * (1 - alpha), as medci() does. It used to use 100 * (1 - alpha / 2), so the default 95% interval was labeled 97.5% CI (and alpha = 0.10 gave 95% CI). The interval itself was always correct. Code that indexes the result by the old name, such as res$"97.5% CI", must use res[[1]] or the new name ("95% CI" at the default alpha) (#123).

Bug fixes

  • dprodnormal() and dprodnormal3() no longer return 0, NA or a silently low density when a factor’s mean is very large relative to its standard error (mu / se above about 3000 for two factors, about 1000 for some three-factor cases). The integrand is a narrow spike there and the fixed integration window missed it. The window is now split at the spike (found from the roots of the conditional mean), with a scaled absolute tolerance for the far subintervals. Values for well-conditioned inputs are unchanged (#117).

Internal

  • Eight tests-only PRs add independent-oracle and planted-defect coverage for the risk files: medci()/ci() endpoints (#115), point masses and |rho| = 1 (#116), pMC()/qMC() closed forms (#118), qprodnormal() (#119, #126), confintAsymp()/confintMC() (#120), .prod3_bound() (#121) and MBCO size and a real-OpenMx check (#122).

RMediation 1.8.1 (2026-10-31)

No change to returned values or to the API.

Documentation

  • The README examples for medci() and ci() on a ProductNormal3 now show the real output of those calls (they showed intervals that the functions do not return), and the Monte Carlo calculator of the online apps is linked.
  • The SEMFit mbco() route is no longer described as experimental: medfit dropped that label in 0.11.0.
  • The pkgdown site gains a Quick Reference, a Cookbook (including serial mediation through medfit, the SEMFit route and omitted-confounder sensitivity) and Technical Notes (the exact CDF at |rho| = 1, point masses, the densities).

Internal

  • Added .lintr (120 columns) and wrapped 61 over-long or mis-indented lines in R sources and tests; the parsed code is unchanged. Rewrapped roxygen lines regenerate seven help pages with the same content.

RMediation 1.8.0 (2026-10-30)

  • S7 property access now works under the declared R 4.1 minimum.

Testing

  • Expanded public OpenMx MBCO argument, bootstrap-routing and optimizer-fallback tests, including result-field mutation checks and fitted RAM smoke tests. Coverage CI now retains line/expression summaries and uncovered-line artifacts.
  • The SEMFit MBCO tests and the mbco() example pass fixed_x and meanstructure to medfit::fit_sem() explicitly, at today’s values, so medfit 0.14.0’s default-change warning does not appear (medfit flips these defaults in 0.15.0). Results are unchanged; the example now needs medfit >= 0.9.0 (#85).

Removed

  • medci_prototype() is removed. It was an exported S7-core prototype of medci() (shipped in 1.6.1) that nothing in the package called. Use medci(), or ci() on a ProductNormal, which return the same intervals.

Bug fixes

  • mbco(type = "parametric") now checks every bootstrap replicate like type = "semi" does. It used to hand the bootstrap to OpenMx::mxCompare(boot = TRUE), so a replicate null fit that violated its constraint (for example OpenMx/OpenMx#433 dropping a zero-Jacobian equality at a replicate’s start) entered the null distribution unchecked and understated its statistic. The package now simulates each replicate from the fitted h0 with OpenMx::mxGenerateData(), fits h0 and h1, refits a violated h0 constraint, and stops with an error of class RMediation_bootstrap_infeasible when it cannot be repaired. Behavior changes: a replicate with a non-finite statistic or an h1 fit worse than its h0 fit now stops the call (mxCompare dropped such replicates; the last check also applies to type = "semi"; a replicate that does not converge is dropped within a 5% bound, see the next entry), and a model without a single raw data set (a covariance-data or multigroup model) is refused before sampling. The observed statistic, df and the result shape are unchanged; seeded p-values differ because the replicates are drawn by a different loop.

  • The DOP CDF (pprodnormal(), qprodnormal(), medci()) is exact at |rho| = 1: it now uses Meeker & Escobar’s (1994) quadratic-root solution instead of integrating a step function, which was wrong by up to 4e-5 and could stop with “the integral is probably divergent”. For |rho| < 1 the integrand is evaluated from the factored quadratic (no cancellation at large means) with the roots as breakpoints, and a roundoff report from integrate() relaxes the tolerance to 1e-8, then 1e-6, instead of failing. All 495 evaluations in the article’s own test domain (means of +/-3e5, |rho| up to 0.99999) now succeed; 10 used to stop with an integrator error.

  • mbco_product_null() stops, with class RMediation_h1_nonconverged, when the full model h1 did not converge or was never run. mbco() warns, with class RMediation_fit_nonconverged, when a supplied h0 or h1 carries an unaccepted OpenMx status; the result is unchanged.

  • Point masses now have the right-continuous CDF. pprodnormal3() returned 0.5 at q == 0 for a product identically equal to 0 (and for a single zero-variance, zero-mean first component); it now returns 1, matching P(XYZ <= q). pprodnormal() with a zero standard error follows the same rule (q >= c lower, q < c upper). Continuous zero-mean distributions still give 0.5 at 0.

  • pprodnormal3() rejects a covariance that is not finite and positive semidefinite, including negative variances at very different scales, instead of clamping negative variances to zero.

  • pprodnormal(lower.tail = FALSE) and qprodnormal(lower.tail = FALSE) with type = "dop" now integrate the upper tail directly instead of computing 1 - P(XY <= q), which cancelled below about 1e-10 (an upper quantile at p = 1e-12 round-tripped to a relative error of 7e-5, and smaller tails could not be resolved). The quantile root finder’s tolerance is tightened from the uniroot() default (1.2e-4) to 1e-12, and the integrand handles |rho| = 1 (a point-mass conditional) without a 0/0. Probabilities below about 1e-22 remain unresolved (the integration window leaves out 1.5e-23).

  • medci(type = "mc") reported MC.Error as SE / n.mc; it is now SE / sqrt(n.mc), the standard error of the simulated mean, as documented elsewhere. Intervals and estimates are unchanged.

  • medci() Monte Carlo and plotting no longer stop with a Cholesky error when the covariance is singular (rho = +/-1 or a zero standard error); type = "dop"/"all" with a zero standard error now fails with an actionable message instead of “non-finite function value”.

  • plot/plotCI must be a single TRUE/FALSE in medci() and ci() (a vector or NA previously failed with an obscure condition error).

  • ci(<ProductNormal>, type = "dop") shared the large-mean defect of #60 through a second copy of the integral (it stopped with “please use type=‘MC’” at mu/se of about 20 where medci() already worked). The S7 core now calls qprodnormalMeeker(), so both paths use one integral.

  • pprodnormal3() (and cdf()/dist_quantile() on ProductNormal3) returned 0 for every q, or an error, when two or three components had zero variance. It now returns the exact answer: a point mass at prod(mean) when all three are fixed, and a scaled normal when exactly one is random (#64).

  • medci() was defined twice, in R/medci.R and R/medci_legacy_backup.R (identical code). The backup sorted later and was the live definition, and ?medci merged both sets of documentation into duplicated Usage, Value and Details sections. The backup file is removed; behavior is unchanged. A test now fails if any top-level function is defined in more than one R/ file.

  • pprodnormal() and qprodnormal() with type = "dop" no longer collapse at large standardized means (pprodnormal(400, 20, 20, 1, 1) returned 8e-7 instead of about 0.507) and are accurate in far tails (previously wrong by up to 4e-6 absolute). Both now share one integral over the support of the conditioning variable at a tight tolerance. The CDF is also clamped to [0, 1], so lower.tail = FALSE can no longer be slightly negative (#60).

New features

  • dprodnormal3(): exact density of the product of three normal variables with any mean vector and positive-definite covariance (the counterpart of pprodnormal3()), computed as a two-dimensional integral that conditions on the first factor and reuses the dprodnormal() integral for the other two. Matches the derivative of pprodnormal3() to about 7 digits.

  • dprodnormal() now resolves very small z at nonzero means (it previously could stop with “the integral is probably divergent”).

  • dprodnormal() is the exact density of the product of two normal random variables (any means, any -1 < rho < 1), completing the d/p/q family. It uses the one-dimensional integral of Rohatgi (Glen et al., 2004) in general and the Bessel-K closed form of Nadarajah and Pogany (2016) when both means are zero; the two agree to near machine precision and each is the other’s test oracle. The density is Inf at exactly 0 (a log singularity).

  • pprodnormal() and qprodnormal() accept a vector q / p and return one probability / quantile per element (a list of two vectors for type = "all"). For type = "MC" all elements share one simulated sample, so the estimates are mutually consistent. Scalar calls are unchanged.

  • ml_omitted_confounder() adds a sensitivity analysis for an omitted confounder of the mediator-outcome relation in two-level (1-1-1) mediation, after Tofighi and Kelley (2016). It returns an MLOmittedConfounder object with print, summary, plot and as.data.frame methods. The default screen keeps only positive-definite grid points, so it does not reproduce the published tables; use screen = "none" for those.

  • mbco(h0, h1, type = "asymp") accepts two fitted medfit SEMFit objects with medfit >= 0.8.0. It returns MBCOResult using stats::anova() without refitting or requiring OpenMx. The restricted fit must come first; df is the actual difference. Active tested bounds refuse an invalid chi-square p-value. Bootstrap types, mixed classes and unused fitting controls error. Existing OpenMx paths and CI integration with medfit >= 0.2.0 are preserved.

  • medfit remains optional in Suggests >= 0.2.0. The SEMFit route needs the GitHub/r-universe medfit release; CRAN medfit 0.3.2 cannot exercise it. This development change does not lift the CRAN submission or development-to-main hold.

  • OpenMx mbco() now checks the constraints of h0 and h1 at the fitted solution (issue #34). The OpenMx default feasibility tolerance (0.05) can leave a constrained fit off the null set and understate the statistic. A returned number now changes in that case: a violated h0 (scaled violation above 1e-6) is refit once at tolerance 1e-8 for all three types, the refit model supplies the observed statistic and the bootstrap, a warning of class RMediation_h0_refit reports the change, and the new refit slot of MBCOResult records it (NULL when no refit was needed). Clean fits and constraint-free models are unchanged. If the refit fails, does not converge or leaves the constraint violated, mbco() stops with an error of class RMediation_h0_refit_failed naming the constraint, instead of returning a statistic from a known-invalid fit. A constraint that cannot be evaluated now errors. See the wrong-branch warning below.

  • OpenMx mbco() now also warns, with class RMediation_constraint_not_enforced and right after RMediation_h0_refit, when the refit ran and h0’s fit was identical to h1’s (statistic 0 before the refit) although a constraint of h0 was violated (issue #84). The constraint may not have been enforced. OpenMx (2.19.1 and later) silently drops an equality constraint whose Jacobian is zero at the starting values (OpenMx/OpenMx#433), for example b1 * b2 == 0 started at zero, and a violation within the feasibility tolerance looks the same; a fitted h0 keeps no starting values, so the warning cannot say which. The statistic and the refit slot are unchanged (the seeded example goes from 0 to 0.0878); for a product null use mbco_product_null(). Bootstrap replicates are refit and checked the same way for both bootstrap types (see the type = "parametric" entry under Bug fixes).

  • mbco(type = "semi") and mbco(type = "parametric") now drop a bootstrap replicate whose fits did not converge instead of stopping at the first one (issue #92). Up to 5% of the R replicates may be dropped; above that the call stops with an error of class RMediation_bootstrap_too_many_dropped (with fewer than 20 replicates none may be dropped). The new dropped slot of MBCOResult reports the count (NULL for results without a bootstrap), and the p-value is the proportion of the kept replicates strictly above the observed statistic, with no (1 + k)/(R + 1) correction: the rule of OpenMx::mxCompare(boot = TRUE), whose denominator was also the kept replicates. Only non-convergence is dropped; an unrepairable constraint violation (RMediation_bootstrap_infeasible), a non-finite statistic and an h1 fit worse than its h0 fit still stop the call. ?mbco states the rule.

  • OpenMx mbco() now warns (class RMediation_constraint_branch) when a feasible, converged h0 is not the constrained optimum of an equality constraint: fixing one of the parameters the constraint depends on at 0 gives a converged, feasible fit with -2LL lower by more than 1e-4 (issue #35). It catches the single-constraint product null that lands on the larger-statistic branch (memory_exp: 221.05 against 0.0831) without parsing the constraint. It runs once per call for every type, costs one extra fit per involved parameter (a constraint with more than 5 is skipped with a message), changes no result, and cannot fail the call. In a simulation (60 seeds at each of three effect sizes) it flagged all 28 wrong-branch fits with no false positives. mbco_product_null() avoids the problem.

  • mbco_product_null(h1, paths, ...) tests a product null (a*b = 0, or a serial product) with OpenMx as an intersection-union test: it fixes each path at 0 in a copy of the fitted full model, runs mbco() on each, and returns the result of the branch with the largest p-value, with the new optional MBCOResult@branch slot naming it. Unlike a single nonlinear constraint such as ind == 0, it cannot land on the larger-statistic branch (issue #35; on memory_exp it returns 0.0831 where one constraint gives 221.05). The p-value is conservative when more than one path is 0. A branch whose fit does not converge is an error naming the branch.

  • For numeric/lavaan formula CIs, MCError now uses SE / sqrt(n.mc), the sampling standard error of the simulated mean. The previous SE / n.mc understated simulation uncertainty. This is not an endpoint error estimate.

  • ci(type = "all", H0 = TRUE) now forwards H0, mu0 and Sigma0 to its Monte Carlo component, preserving the alternative/null result pair rather than silently ignoring the requested null distribution.

  • OpenMx MBCO now rejects equal-df and reversed model pairs, and nonfinite or negative observed statistics, before bootstrap sampling. Previously the semiparametric route could report a significant result with df 0 or -1. The restricted model must be supplied first; substantive nesting is still the analyst’s responsibility.

  • OpenMx bootstrap workers now restore global options on success and error. Semiparametric bootstrap rejects failed refits and nonfinite statistics, with explicit errors for singular sample or null covariances. Parametric bootstrap rejects invalid reported statistics, degrees of freedom and p-values.

  • mbco() no longer rejects fitted OpenMx RAM models with “h0 must be an MxModel”. The check compared class(h0) to "MxModel", which fails for subclasses such as MxRAMModel; it now uses methods::is(). Verified for type = "asymp" only; the bootstrap types ("parametric", "semi") have not been exercised on fitted RAM models (rmediation#35).

  • The ?mbco example had shifted path labels (endVar started with "x", so the labels a1, a2, cp landed on the wrong paths) and passed a tibble to mxData(). Both are fixed. The example now tests a1 * b1 = 0 with one linear null per path (a1 == 0, b1 == 0) and reports the smaller statistic (0.0831), because a single nonlinear ind1 == 0 null can converge to the wrong branch (221.05) (rmediation#35).

Documentation

  • ?mbco now has a Details section on testing a product null (a*b = 0): fit one linear null per path and report the smaller statistic, because a single nonlinear null can converge to the wrong branch. It also says to build h0 from the unfitted model, since a constraint refit from the fitted model’s estimates can stop at an infeasible point (diffLL 0) (rmediation#35).

Tests

  • Added a known-answer OpenMx fixture on memory_exp (linear nulls a1 == 0: 221.045546 and b1 == 0: 0.083100) and an end-to-end mbco() test against it.

RMediation 1.7.0 (2026-08-16)

Correctness fix: pprodnormal3() on ill-conditioned covariance (#27)

pprodnormal3() (and its alias p_prod3()) returned materially wrong probabilities when the (X, Y) covariance block was ill-conditioned, silently and with no diagnostic. At rho = 0.999 the error reached 24% at q = 0.5, and 92% in relative terms in the lower tail. Tightening tol did not help – the old integrator converged to a stable but incorrect value. Because cdf(), dist_quantile(), confint() and ci() invert this CDF by root-finding, all of them inherited the error.

  • The default integration method is now "gauss" – tensor-product Gauss-Legendre quadrature on a domain partitioned at the coordinate axes, with the node count escalated automatically until successive rules agree to tol. Partitioning is what makes a fixed-grid rule valid here: the integrand has a kink along both axes, and an unpartitioned grid can return values outside [0, 1].

  • This changes results. On well-conditioned input the new default agrees with the old one to about 1e-6. On ill-conditioned input it differs substantially – that difference is the correction. The new method is also faster (roughly 8-20x at the covariances tested).

  • method = "hcubature" selects the previous integrator, retained for cross-checking and backward comparison. It is not recommended when the (X, Y) block is ill-conditioned.

  • The error figures above were measured at q = 0.5 with mean = c(0.2, 0.1, 0) on one family of covariance matrices: unit variances, correlation 0.5 between Z and each of X and Y, and rho between X and Y in {0.5, 0.99, 0.999, 0.9999}. The reference value was a 1024-node Gauss-Legendre rule that agreed with the 512-node rule to 3e-7 or better and lay within 3 standard errors of a 1e7-draw Monte Carlo check. The magnitudes describe that family: the error is not a monotone function of the condition number across arbitrary covariance matrices, and a well-conditioned matrix can show a smaller error than an ill-conditioned one.

  • New nodes argument forces a fixed number of Gauss-Legendre nodes per dimension instead of escalating adaptively.

  • New diagnostics argument. When TRUE, the returned value carries "error" (the gap between the last two quadrature rules – a real convergence estimate) and "nodes" attributes. It defaults to FALSE so the return value stays a bare numeric for existing callers. The meaning of "error" differs by method and is NA when nodes is supplied; see ?pprodnormal3 for the per-method contract.

  • pprodnormal3() now warns when quadrature reaches the node cap without meeting tol, instead of returning a wrong answer silently. The warning reports the gap between the last two rules, which bounds the remaining discretization error, and does not assert a cause: a well-conditioned covariance reaches the cap too when tol is tighter than 2048 nodes can deliver (issue #31).

  • Fixed: the documented ProductNormal3() constructor call raised an error. The method property had no default, and the validator rejected the resulting empty value, so the form shown in the README and the getting-started vignette –

    ProductNormal3(mu = mu, Sigma = Sigma)
#> Error: method must be 'hcubature'

    – failed for anyone who copied it. method now defaults to "gauss", and the call works as documented. Passing method explicitly was, and remains, a valid alternative.

  • The new default also fixes a second, previously unreported failure of the old integrator: at large standardized means (mean / sd beyond roughly 8) it returned exactly 0 where the true probability is around 0.46. That failure was independent of conditioning and equally silent.

RMediation 1.6.1 (2026-06-30)

CRAN release: 2026-07-21

Naming convention cleanup

  • p_prod3() is renamed to pprodnormal3() to match the existing pprodnormal()/qprodnormal() family. p_prod3() remains available as a silent (non-warning) alias and will gain a formal deprecation warning in a future release.

  • ProductNormal2() remains available but is superseded by ProductNormal() for direct construction; internal callers now use ProductNormal() directly.

  • The ci() generic’s dispatch argument is renamed from mu to object for consistency with the package’s other S7 generics (cdf(), dist_quantile()). This only affects callers using ci(mu = ...) as a named argument; positional calls (ci(mu, ...)) are unaffected.

  • Undocumented internal helpers (validate_ProductNormal(), is_valid_for_computation(), ProductNormal_from_lavaan()) are now hidden from the package documentation index (@noRd); they remain available internally but are not part of the public API.

    Old New
    p_prod3(q, mean, cov, ...) pprodnormal3(q, mean, cov, ...)
    ci(mu = ..., Sigma = ..., quant = ...) ci(..., Sigma = ..., quant = ...) (positional)

Documentation and lint

  • Added @examples to all exported functions/generics that previously lacked them, addressing goodpractice::gp() advisories ahead of CRAN resubmission.

RMediation 1.6.0 (2026-06-29)

ProductNormal3: exact CDF for the product of three normals

  • New S7 class ProductNormal3 for sequential indirect effects of the form a1 * a2 * b, with print(), cdf(), confint(), and ci() methods.
  • New core engine p_prod3() computes P(a1 * a2 * b <= q) via the conditional-expectation dimension-reduction double integral (Tofighi, 2026).
  • Integration is performed by cubature::hcubature; degenerate covariances are reduced to the existing two-variable product-normal CDF.

Dependencies

  • Added cubature (>= 2.1.0) to Imports.

RMediation 1.5.0 (2026-06-18)

CRAN release: 2026-06-20

Dependencies

  • medfit is now available on CRAN (v0.2.0/0.2.1). Removed Remotes: data-wise/medfit; medfit now resolves from CRAN. Pinned Suggests: medfit (>= 0.2.0).

medfit Covariance Extraction

  • ci() for medfit MediationData/SerialMediationData now extracts the path covariance by parameter name and uses the full covariance matrix (including off-diagonals) for both simple and serial mediation. Removed the previous positional/value-matching heuristics and the independence/diagonal fallbacks, which could silently produce incorrect intervals; unresolved path labels now raise an informative error.
  • The serial-mediation pipeline is now verified end-to-end against medfit’s released serial extractor (medfit >= 0.2.0): medfit::extract_mediation() produces a SerialMediationData for both lavaan (ordered mediator vector) and lm/glm (mediator_models) chains, and ci() consumes it via the documented d1, d2, ... path-name contract. Added integration tests that fit a real model, extract, and run ci() end-to-end (skipped when medfit < 0.2.0).

RMediation 1.4.0

Major Changes

S7 Core Architecture (Complete Refactoring)

  • Complete architectural redesign: S7 is now the computational core, with legacy functions as thin wrappers.
  • Zero breaking changes: All existing code continues to work exactly as before (100% backward compatible).
  • Enhanced extensibility: New computational architecture makes adding CI methods and features straightforward.

S7 OOP Classes

  • Introduced S7 object-oriented programming for modern, type-safe class definitions.
  • New S7 Classes:
    • ProductNormal: Represents the distribution of the product of normal random variables.
    • MBCOResult: Encapsulates results from MBCO tests.
  • New S7 Generics: cdf(), dist_quantile(), ci(), print(), summary(), show().
  • All S7 classes include comprehensive display methods (print, summary, show) for meaningful output.

N-Variable Product Support (NEW)

  • Breaking limitation removed: Can now compute confidence intervals for products of 3 or more variables.
  • Works with Monte Carlo method (type = "mc").
  • Example: ProductNormal(mu = c(0.3, 0.4, 0.5), Sigma = diag(3)) for three-way products.
  • Previous versions limited to 2-variable products only.

Internal Computational Core

  • New internal S7 functions: .compute_ci_dop(), .compute_ci_mc(), .compute_ci_asymp(), .compute_cdf_dop(), .compute_cdf_mc(), .compute_quantile_dop(), .compute_quantile_mc().
  • All core algorithms now work with ProductNormal objects natively.
  • Legacy functions (medci(), pprodnormal(), qprodnormal()) convert parameters and dispatch to S7 core.
  • Identical numerical results to previous versions (validated with 201 tests).

Enhanced ci() Function

  • Migrated ci() to S7 generic with methods for:
    • numeric: Legacy support for direct coefficient/covariance input.
    • lavaan: Automatic extraction and CI computation for indirect effects.
    • ProductNormal: Native S7 class support.
  • Auto-detection: Automatically identifies product parameters (e.g., ab := a*b) in lavaan models.
  • Renamed first argument to mu for better legacy compatibility.

MBCO Function Updates

  • Migrated mbco() to S7 generic with method for MxModel objects.
  • Returns MBCOResult S7 objects with properties: statistic, df, p_value, type.
  • Legacy Compatibility: Implemented S3 methods ($, [[, names) for backward-compatible list-style access (e.g., result$chisq, result$p).
  • Display methods show significance indicators (, , , ns) and interpretation.

Input Validation

  • Comprehensive input validation using checkmate package across all functions.
  • Type checking with match.arg() for categorical arguments.
  • Improved error messages for invalid inputs.

Display Methods

  • All S7 classes have meaningful print(), summary(), and show() methods.
  • ProductNormal displays: distribution type, means, covariance matrix, SDs, and correlations.
  • MBCOResult displays: test type, statistics, p-values with significance levels, and interpretation.

Namespace Improvements

  • Zero masking warnings: Package now loads cleanly with no namespace conflicts.
  • Renamed quantile() generic to dist_quantile() to avoid masking stats::quantile().
  • S7 methods for print(), summary(), show() now properly register with base generics.
  • Added S4 compatibility via S7::S4_register() for formal generic support.

Package Cleanup

  • Removed unused dependencies (doParallel, foreach, methods).
  • Fixed all documentation warnings and notes.
  • R CMD check: Now passes with 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.
  • Added 40 new S7 prototype tests + 19 display method tests (total: 201 tests, 100% pass rate).

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed argument dispatch issues between alpha and level parameters.
  • Resolved S7 generic conflicts with base R functions (print, summary, quantile).
  • Fixed recursive dispatch issues in display methods.
  • Added case-insensitive handling for type parameter (accepts “MC”, “mc”, “DOP”, “dop”, etc.).
  • Fixed return value structure for ci() method (now returns list with CI, Estimate, SE components).
